subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (latency / cost / quality)
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (latency / cost / quality)

Hi Lina & Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the model shortlist we discussed for your summarization + entity-extraction workflow. High level notes from the call:

- Goal: replace current internal NER pipeline for docs ingestion and surface concise executive summaries; target P95 latency <= 400ms for single-doc requests, and batch throughput for nightly jobs.
- Data: mixed-length docs (1-10k tokens), some PII present; retention/legal constraints mean logs must be auditable.
- Success metrics: precision of extracted entities >= 92% on our seed evals; ROUGE-L improvement vs baseline for summaries; cost target: < $300 / 1M input tokens (total inference cost).

Recommended shortlist (tradeoff rationale below):

1) open-model-x-13b-quant (default recommendation)
   - Rationale: best cost/quality balance for your docs. 13B quantized runs with Redwood-optimized kernels; we saw near-parity to larger 70B models on extraction accuracy with substantially lower latency and cost.
   - Estimated P95 latency (single-doc, p2-standard equiv): ~220-280ms.
   - Estimated cost: ~$95 / 1M tokens (inference only).

2) open-model-y-70b-flash-attn (high-quality, higher-cost)
   - Rationale: stronger summarization and reasoning out-of-the-box for complex docs; useful for highest-quality reports and edge-case extraction.
   - Estimated P95 latency: ~650-900ms.
   - Estimated cost: ~$420 / 1M tokens.

3) distilled-open-7b + Redwood caching profile (low-latency, low-cost)
   - Rationale: for endpoints where sub-100ms tail latency matters (inline UI experiences). Accuracy is slightly lower; good for low-cost routing for straightforward docs.
   - Estimated P95 latency: ~80-140ms.
   - Estimated cost: ~$28 / 1M tokens.

We generally recommend starting with open-model-x-13b-quant for a pilot: it hits your quality target on the seed prompt set we ran, and keeps latency and costs comfortably within your targets for most single-doc requests. For critical reports, route to open-model-y-70b. For UI preview and high-concurrency endpoints, use distilled-open-7b. Redwood routing policies can automate fallback (e.g., if 13B fails quality checks, escalate to 70B).

Attached: quick benchmark CSV of the runs we did during the demo and the prompt set we used (prompt-set-acme-v1.jsonl). Also linking the shared evaluation sheet in Drive.

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood: provision a short 2-week pilot environment with access to the 13B quant and 70B variants (we can provide a dedicated test key + preconfigured eval harness).
- Acme: share a small evaluation corpus (50-100 representative documents) or give us access to a sanitized sample.
- Set a sync next week (30 min) to finalize routing rules and SLOs.

Would you like us to provision the pilot this week? If yes, we’ll spin up the test endpoints and push the prompt set + a runbook for the eval.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple quick Qs from our side before we kick off the pilot: 

1) P95 latency: our UX team will only accept up to 400ms for single-doc inline summaries. Your numbers look great for 13B — can you confirm the test hardware you measured P95 on and whether that includes network overhead for our region (we're on us-west)?

2) Regarding quality/regression monitoring: what's the suggested approach to catch quality regressions during rolling updates? We'd like to avoid surprises once in production.

3) For the pilot: can you spin up a test endpoint with request-level logging disabled by default (we're still sorting legal on what we can share)?

Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (latency / cost / quality)

Great questions — answers inline below. I’m copying Avery (solutions lead) and Dev (SE) so we can action provisioning.

1) P95 latency specifics:
   - Benchmark hardware: our numbers are from a standard benchmark on a c6g-equivalent GPU node (Redwood Dedicated p2-equivalent). The latencies quoted include end-to-end model runtime + Redwood runtime overhead but exclude inter-region network latency. For us-west customers we typically see an additional ~25-45ms network overhead depending on client setup. So your expected P95 for open-model-x-13b-quant in us-west is ~245-325ms — still under your 400ms target in most cases.

2) Quality/regression monitoring:
   - Recommended approach: we push a lightweight eval harness that runs your seed prompt set (the 50-100 docs) against any candidate model (or model weights) during canary and rolling deploys. Redwood can auto-block a rollout if evaluation metrics (precision/ROUGE-L) drop below configured thresholds. We also provide per-prompt diffs and a quality dashboard that surfaces regressions and example failures.

3) Pilot logging and data controls:
   - We can provision the pilot with request/response logging disabled by default. For the pilot you'll get a private test key and a short runbook to toggle logging. If you need encrypted-at-rest logs or specific retention windows, we can enable those in the Private deployment or Dedicated offering.

Provisioning plan (proposed):
- Today/Tomorrow: Acme shares sanitized 50-doc sample.
- 48 hours after sample: Redwood spins up endpoints (13B-quant + 70B) under a test key. We'll run the seed eval and share the results.
- Week 1: iterate on prompts & routing rules; set alert thresholds.

Avery / Dev — can you confirm availability to provision the 13B quant container for the pilot? Also, I'll need a short note on quota and an expected cost estimate for a 2-week pilot (we typically do a $X estimate; fine to give a range).

Lina/Tom — if you confirm the sample drop timing, we’ll proceed to provision.

Thanks —
Marissa
